chapter: Spirits of Rhythm and the road in the 1930s
title: When the Spirits first reached California; where the film was made
summary: Bunn says he came west in 1940, passed through earlier without stopping, and worked with Ethel Waters back east.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So you came out to California way back then. About '33?
I came out here in 1940.
But I mean, when you were on tour, were you here before then, on tour?
No. Yeah. Was I? Wait a minute, now.
Would you like to have a beer?
I'd love one, yeah, thanks.
Excuse me for interrupting.
That's okay.
You're bringing up things now that I don't know. But you must be studying that book, whatever you've got.
Well, it's all, you know, bits and pieces.
Yeah.
But I've been trying to get a clear
picture of different things.
Yeah. Well, I'd be glad to tell you if I knew. Because, you know, it's been so long.
Well, can you remember like some of the places that the Spirits played, you know? Besides New York, of course. But you must have gone out on the road with the Spirits, the original Spirits.
Yeah. Out here. We hit here after New York.
Uh-huh.
We hit California.
But was that in 1940?
Yeah.
You didn't come out before then, then?
No, we come out -- I was through here, but didn't stop.
I see. When was -- you made the film, though.
Huh?
Where did you make the film, then? Maybe the film was made back East.
Which one?
That film with Ethel Waters.
Let's see.
Because they had movie studios back here for awhile, you know, in New Jersey, I think, in the '20s and the early '30s.
Wow. I didn't come out here with Ethel. I was back east with Ethel.
Uh-huh.
